name: Anderson Front Squat
description: A front squat performed from a dead stop with the barbell resting on safety pins inside a power rack, starting from the bottom position. Eliminating the stretch reflex removes elastic energy contribution and forces the lifter to generate strength from a fully stopped position, targeting the sticking point of the squat.

execution.starting_position: Set safety pins inside a power rack at a height corresponding to the bottom of your front squat. Bar rests on the pins. Duck under and take the front rack position.
execution.setup_instructions: Set safety pins at the correct height for your squat depth. Load the bar on the pins, then position yourself under it in the front rack before beginning each rep.
steps: Step 1: Position yourself under the bar in the front rack with elbows high.
Step 2: Brace your core hard from a complete dead-stop position.
Step 3: Drive through your legs to lift the bar off the pins and ascend to full lockout.
Step 4: Lower the bar back to the pins with control. Reset and repeat.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale and brace fully before each individual rep. Exhale at lockout.
common_mistakes: Rushing the start — ensure a full brace before each lift off the pins
Dropping the elbows and losing the front rack during the lift
safety_considerations: Use significantly less weight than your regular front squat — no stretch reflex means much less force production
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full extension at lockout. Bottom position is predetermined by pin height.
coaching_cues: Elbows stay high through the entire lift
